A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SpargeAttention work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendix A.1–A.4. The additional v8 page contains a reference continuation; the appendix content matches after accounting for pagination.

before.justification: v7 reports original language, image, and video generation evaluations, attention benchmarks, ablations, and appendix sparsity analyses.

after.justification: v8 retains original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix A, including model quality, latency, ablation, and sparsity measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain selective token compression, both masking stages, sparse warp online softmax, SageAttention integration, and HilbertCurve permutation without procedural changes.

E1.justification: Section 4.1 and the appendices retain the same WikiText, LongBench, InfiniteBench En.MC, Needle-in-a-Haystack, COCO, and Open-Sora prompt evaluations across the same language, image, and video models.

E2.justification: MInference and FlexPrefill remain the sparse baselines in Tables 1 and 11. Table 2 and Figure 10 also retain their comparator sets; the added related-work citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the stated speed metric from TOPS to inverse latency 1/t and specifies t in seconds; Table 1 and Figure 10 adopt the new label. However, the formula retains O(attn)/t and appendix Table 11 retains TOPS. This is an inconsistent reported metric revision, with no evidence of rerunning experiments or changing other settings.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix A retain the same prediction-overhead, permutation, self-similarity, mask-contribution, sequence-length, and diffusion sparsity analyses, with unchanged supporting evidence.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty estimates, or statistical testing procedures are added or revised. Appendix A.2 retains the same threshold-based case selection, and the appendix averaging practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted curves, rankings, and qualitative examples are retained throughout both PDFs. For example, Table 1 retains SpargeAttn's Llama3.1 NIAH score of 0.909, and Table 2 retains its Mochi latency of 1037 seconds. The changed speed labels provide no new measurements or evidence of a performance gain.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 changes the displayed speed definition from TOPS = O(attn)/t to 1/t = O(attn)/t. Because O(attn) remains defined as the operation count, this introduces a mathematically inconsistent equality. The attention definitions and derivations are otherwise unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of universal, training-free sparse and quantized attention, preserved end-to-end quality, and substantial acceleration. The contribution and novelty claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations concerning relevant-information selection, permutation robustness, and sparsity variation across sequence lengths, layers, heads, and timesteps remain unchanged. No substantive limitations or applicability qualifications are added.

D1.justification: CUDA implementation information, hyperparameter thresholds, block sizes, permutation instructions, hardware disclosures, and code-access information remain unchanged, including the first-page note about the SageAttention2 implementation.

R1.justification: v8 adds Zhang et al.'s survey of efficient attention methods and removes Deng et al. (2024), replacing the latter's sparsity citation. Section 2 also expands quantization citations to the already referenced SageAttention2, SageAttention2++, and SageAttention3. The overall taxonomy and research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to citation-bearing passages, speed-metric wording, and the version/date stamp. The title, abstract, section order, method exposition, and appendix organization are retained without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Table 1 changes its speed headers and slightly adjusts column widths; Figure 10 changes its vertical-axis label from TOPS to 1/t. Minor text and reference reflow creates a nearly blank reference-continuation page in v8. All figures and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v8 makes speed reporting less consistent: Section 4.1 equates inverse latency with operation count divided by latency, Table 1 and Figure 10 retain their numbers under the new label, and appendix Table 11 still reports TOPS. This impairs interpretation of absolute speed measurements without explaining a conversion. The limited citation updates do not offset this defect. Unchanged methods, quality results, and end-to-end latencies limit the overall deterioration.
